p.t: In short
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: Do not start a business with friends or family as partners. The only exception is paid, project-based specialist work.
Write a contract before any work starts. It must say who does what and how a partner can be removed.

Build your first store alone before you bring in partners or hire people for daily work.
Pick one method at a time, and ask questions early, so problems get solved.
Deciding whether to take a business partner
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: **Avoid** business partnerships with friends or family members.
The exception is a family member who does paid, project-based specialist work, such as graphic design or web design. That is acceptable.
Partnerships are hard to keep working.
**Write a contract** before any work starts. It must define each partner's responsibilities.
Include clauses (written rules inside the contract) for buyout (one partner buys out the other) or removal if a partner does not deliver. Older (2021).
**Avoid** managing partners and equity partnerships early. A managing partner runs the business day to day. An equity partnership means a partner owns a share of the company.
Roles and effort often become unbalanced once a store takes off, and partners can fall out.
**Build the store** from zero to one (from nothing to a first working store) with your own effort first. Then outsource (pay others to do) the day-to-day work. Older (2021).
The partnership model can be repeated several times with different people. This creates multiple extra income streams (extra sources of money).
Overseeing **5 to 10 or more** stores this way avoids working 8 to 12 hours a day running each one yourself.
Sources differ in emphasis. The caution against early equity partnerships applies to your first store. The repeatable partnership model applies when you expand beyond one store.
Partnering to run several stores at once is a **higher-risk** expansion than building one store alone.
It offers a larger payoff if it succeeds, but the outcome is uncertain.
**Two people working as a team** who find synergy (good teamwork that adds up to more than each person alone) tend to perform very well. They move faster than solo operators.
**Choose** business partners, suppliers and collaborators as carefully as you would choose close friends.
They shape the quality of your daily work and the time you have left for it.
Choosing partners
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: When choosing partners to run stores, **prioritize** people who have completed proper training, have already made a first sale, and are fully committed.
If the program requires it, also check that they are willing to relocate (move) to the operating location.
**Surround yourself** with people who are more talented than you in their areas. Your output tends to match the quality of the people and inputs around you.
If you are the most talented person in your group, look for a group where you can learn more.
Define each partner's role **in writing**, so that responsibilities do not overlap or fall through the gaps.

Define roles with this procedure:
1. List what each partner is good at and what each is not good at.
2. Assign ownership (who is responsible for what) accordingly.
3. Use personality type, such as introvert (prefers quiet, focused work) or extrovert (prefers talking and meeting people).
Use it to decide who handles outreach (contacting people) and who handles ads and back-end work (behind-the-scenes tasks customers do not see).
Give each partner **their own area** and the freedom to decide within it, so they do not need to approve every small choice.
Escalate (pass up to the group) only decisions that affect the shared plan or money.

Partners do not need to report every routine action, such as a refund (money returned to a customer), to each other.
Escalate only **significant decisions and changes**.
Partners in a small business should be willing to take on tasks outside their formal role when needed.
**Share equally** the workload and the stress of the business between partners. Do not let one person carry it.
**Schedule** important business conversations at a set time on a workday, not in social or family settings.
Before the conversation, prepare the proposed solution, the reasons for it, and its pros and cons (advantages and disadvantages). Then a decision can be made quickly.
Working with family members
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: Give family members clear rules and a **written job description** before they start working, the same as any other hire.
Family work benefits from explicit expectations, meaning expectations that are clearly stated.

Working with family can work well. **Set the rules first** and treat the arrangement as a business relationship.
Avoid vague arrangements that make it hard to ask for results.
The exception for contracted specialized services is covered under "Deciding whether to take a business partner."
Growth in dropshipping (selling products that a supplier ships straight to the customer,
so you hold no stock) depends on **three resources**. These are a coach, virtual assistants (remote helpers), and continuous education (ongoing learning).
Plan for all three as the business scales (grows).

An outside coach (an expert who is not on your team) who audits (checks) the whole store and gives you a prioritized task list (tasks ranked by importance) can produce a **quick sales lift** (a fast rise in

sales).
In one case, **nearly $6,000** more in monthly sales came after the first coaching call.

A coach's advice is that learning is best when you **focus on one approach** and avoid switching between too many tools.
Once a process works, keep it.
Mentor programs
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: A mentor is an experienced guide. To join the Mentor Program, log into the members area, click "Get Help," then select "Private Mentorship."

**No application** is required.
**Book weekly 30-minute** one-on-one video calls with mentors who earn a minimum of $100,000 per month. Older (2022).
Choose mentors by **specialty**: paid traffic (visitors who come from paid ads), Google Shopping (product ads on Google), Facebook, conversion optimization (getting more visitors to buy),
supplier relationships, exclusivity negotiation (agreeing that a supplier sells only to you), pricing terms, or web design. Older (2022).
Select based on your specific needs that week. Older (2022).
A weekly 30-minute accountability call (a regular check-in where someone tracks your progress) with the mentor is worth it.
This is true even when there is little to discuss, because it keeps progress on track. Older (2022).
Pooling unused call credits (unused call allowances) across months is **not practical** with current booking systems. Older (2022).
Monthly coaching accountability includes **defining specific action items** for the next 30 days. Older (2021-2022).
At the next call, review completion status, obstacles (things blocking you), and reasons for incomplete items. Older (2021-2022).
In the Master Plan 12-month structure, each client **selects** when to schedule their monthly coaching session within the upcoming month. Dates are not assigned to them. Older (2021-2022).
Members can work with different coaches from the Dropship Breakthrough team for individual sessions. These include founder John, coach Ben, and other available coaches. Older (2021-2022).
Mentors usually answer student questions within **one hour**, or within 48 hours when they are traveling.
Send questions in advance through a form before group calls so the mentor can prepare answers.

One call per week is the **standard during the build phase** (the early stage of setting up the store).
Calls can be spaced further apart depending on progress.

Several calls per week are only useful in the scaling phase (the growth stage). This is when ads are live, sales are coming in, and decisions about Facebook ad campaigns (groups of ads run together) are needed.
Source D support structure
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: Effective program support combines **three layers**: a personal pod (a small private group with a coach and a Client Success Manager),

a shared community channel for general questions, and scheduled live Q&A calls.
Together, they make sure a participant always has a clear route to get help.
In a personal pod, each participant gets a dedicated coach with real operating experience at six-figure revenue (**$100,000 or more** in revenue).
Each participant also gets a Client Success Manager (CSM) whose job is to keep the participant on track with their plan.
The CSM role is about **follow-through** (finishing what was planned) and accountability, not only answering questions.
A weekly live group call is a working session. Students bring their numbers, ads, product pages and stuck points, and the coach reviews them in real time (as they happen).
The purpose is to **unblock students** (remove what is stopping them) each week, not to sell.
Combining one-on-one guidance, group knowledge and live call support gives you personalized answers for your business. It also gives you the benefit of collective experience.

This combination shows you the **next concrete step** to take.
The Source D community has revenue-based tiers (membership levels based on monthly sales).
Members **move up** when they hit the next milestone. Each move assigns them a coach who specializes in that revenue stage.

**Beginner**: Just starting, no sales yet
**First sale achieved**: First sale completed
**$500/Day Club**: $500 per day in sales

**$5k/Month Club**: $5,000 per month in sales
**$10k/Month Club**: $10,000 per month in sales
**$30k/Month Club**: $30,000 per month in sales
**$100k+/Month Elite Builders Club**: $100,000+ per month in sales
Do not hold back questions because you fear they are too basic or that you will speak up in a group.
**Asking early** is what gets problems solved. The team can only help with struggles that are reported.
Consuming all the material without asking questions hides real problems. The support team cannot see that you are stuck.
**Raise struggles** in the pod, the community or the calls as soon as they appear.
Booking calls (continued)
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: Booking calls
Older (2021-2022). Follow these steps:
1. **Open** the booking link for coaching sessions. It is the same link for every call, and it is also sent in your confirmation email.
2. **Look** at the calendar. Days with available slots are highlighted in blue. **Click** one.
3. **Check** the time zone (the local clock setting for your region) shown above the times. It is detected automatically.

If you will be in another time zone, open the time zone dropdown (a menu of zones) and choose a different one.
4. **Select** a time slot in the panel to the right of the calendar.

5. **Click** the blue Confirm button.
6. **Enter** your Name and Email. Both are required.
7. Optional: **write** something in the field "Please share anything that will help prepare for our meeting."

8. Optional: **enter** your mobile number to receive SMS reminders (text message alerts). The country code is preselected based on your location.
9. **Click** Schedule Event.
The one-to-one booking link is listed in the course's resources section. It is also sent in the booking confirmation email.

The same link is used for every one-to-one call, so it **does not need to be requested again**.
A booked coaching call lasts **one hour** and is listed as "1 hr" on the booking page.

Coaching calls are held on Zoom (a video call app).
The Zoom link is provided **only after booking is confirmed**. It is sent in the meeting confirmation email.

Available slots are offered in **30-minute** increments (steps).
Every slot shown can be booked directly, with no need to ask the coach beforehand.
The booking page is connected to all of the coach's calendars. Only times the coach has marked as available are shown.

If an expected time does not appear, it is already booked and cannot be selected.
The booking page detects your time zone automatically and shows times in it.
Booking a one-to-one coaching call (continued)
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t:
To change it, use the time zone dropdown, which has a search field.
This is useful when traveling or when booking for a future time zone.

The dropdown also offers an am/pm or 24h (24-hour clock) time format toggle (switch).
Name and email are **mandatory** on the booking form.

The email address is needed to send the meeting confirmation with the call link. The booking cannot be completed without it.
The preparation field is **optional**.

A pre-coaching survey (a short questionnaire) is sent afterward, after booking. It asks which topics to cover and what to share about the business. So the free-text field does not have to be filled in.

SMS reminders are **optional**. Enter the mobile number in the "Send text messages to" field.
The country code loads automatically based on your location and can be changed.

The form has an optional "Add Guests" field below the preparation box.
It is **not required** to complete the booking.
After Schedule Event, the call is added to the coach's calendar and to your own calendar.
The confirmation email then contains the booking link and all details needed to join at the booked time.
After booking is confirmed, the confirmation page tells you to join the call with the **Zoom link** from your booking confirmation or calendar entry.
The page also shows the booked time with the time zone name, so you can check it before the call.
Book your own coaching calls through the members area.
Go to Blueprint, hover over "Activate" (move your mouse over it), click "Activate Coaching," then select available times.

**You choose** when to schedule. Calls are not pre-assigned by the company. Older (2022).
Call lengths differ by program. Source B's one-to-one coaching calls last **one hour**.

Source A's mentor calls are **30 minutes** each.
Check the length shown when you book.
Peer networks and masterminds
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: **Work with your community** instead of alone.

Talk to others in the same position, learn from their mistakes, and lift each other up together.
Solo work is significantly harder and less effective.
From the start, talk with peers about campaigns and goals.
Use Google Ads support (Google's help for its paid ads), Quora (a question-and-answer website), Facebook groups, private forums and masterminds.
Get advice from other ecommerce entrepreneurs (people who sell online) **without needing to share your store**.
Peer networks help you learn the same tools and logic, and can lead to partnerships.
A mastermind group (a small group that meets to share ideas and solve problems together) should be a **small private group of 2 to 5 people**.
Ideally, its members are owners who each spend less than **$1,000 per month** on Google Ads.

Members share information and work together on scaling profitable campaigns.
Online marketing is competitive.
A supportive group of peers makes the workload feel easier. It also helps keep momentum (forward speed) during scaling.
Joining a community of established store owners is a practical way to get a **second set of eyes** on a store.
For example, the community can give a peer review of the homepage (the front page of the website) and the policy pages (rules pages such as returns and shipping).
Brand ambassadors are fans who promote your brand. Build their community through a private Facebook group, with reasons to join such as brand appeal, a social cause, and rewards.
Aim to grow it to about **20,000 members**. About 3,000 had been reached at the time of writing.
Discord and live calls
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: Discord is a chat app with topic channels.
Use its community channels and monthly coaching calls to stay engaged, ask questions, and maintain accountability while executing your scaling plan.
Source A live group coaching calls are held on the **first Wednesday** of each month at 2 PM EST (Eastern Standard Time, a US time zone).

The calls are hosted on Discord. Attendance is included in the membership as a bonus.
All live coaching calls are recorded.
Replays (recordings to watch later) of the previous **three months** are available. Missed calls can be watched within that window.
Source D live Q&A calls (question-and-answer sessions) take place **every Thursday at 8 p.m. Singapore Time (SGT)** in the Voice channel of the Discord community.
Weekly Source D Q&A calls cover common roadblocks, advanced strategies to scale faster, and live reviews of stores, ads and funnels (the step-by-step paths customers follow to buy).
You can ask anything in real time and receive direct feedback from the mentors.
Sources differ on schedule because they cover different programs. Source A's live calls run monthly on the first Wednesday. Source D Q&A runs weekly on Thursdays.
**Follow the schedule** of the program you belong to.
Source D uses Discord as the community hub (the main meeting place).
The general community channel holds shared insights, updates and wins. The Voice channel hosts the live Q&A calls.
If the general channel is not visible after joining, **report it to support right away**.
Take personal and detailed questions about your own business to your small pod group. That is where you receive feedback specific to your situation.
Post broad questions, such as what is currently working in ads or tips for choosing suppliers, in the main community channel.
There you can learn from the combined experience of many operators (people who run stores), not only from the coach.
Where to ask what (continued)
p.s: Business partners, mentors and community support

p.t: The shared community draws on the experiences of **more than 100** other operators. You can learn from many peers and not only from your assigned coach.

This is most useful for broad, current questions.
**Use the chat** to share community wins rather than reposting questions.
Conversations that include wins are encouraged in the share-your-wins channel.
Check Discord channel retention times (how long posts are kept) in the Welcome channel.
The social and for-sale channels clear their posts. The topic channels are kept.
Use the members area Bonuses section to find past coaching call replays and the links mentioned in them.
Shopify (a platform for building online stores) runs a Discord-based 100K club.

It is open only to stores that have already done more than **$100,000 in sales**.
Store owners below that threshold should not expect access yet.

The 100K club is a peer group on the course's Discord.
Stores can apply to join once they have done more than $100,000 in sales.

Eligibility is based on **sales volume**, not on time in business.
Member community rule: the 100K community is for store owners who have done at least $100,000 in sales.

Use it for peer questions alongside coach answers.
Sources differ on the threshold wording. Two sources say "more than $100,000". One says "at least $100,000".
**Confirm the current rule** with the community before applying, if your sales are exactly at $100,000.

New member onboarding in an online ecommerce community:
1. **Create** your Shopify store first, using the trial link provided in the community.
2. **Join** the Discord server and open a private support ticket. This is where support, coaching and progress tracking happen.
3. In the ticket, **introduce yourself** with your name, your goals, and whether you are completely new or already experienced. This makes sure the right helper is assigned.

4. **Send** a short greeting in the welcome channel to unlock the other channels.
5. **Open** the course and start with the first part, then work through the parts in order.
